messages.subject_clean: Value distance shows NA in nearest neighborhood matching
messages.body_plain:
Hello Everyone,

I am trying to use the data nuclearplants from the library optmatch to 
do the matching.
library(optmatch) # for data nuclearplants
library (MatchIt) # for matching
data(nuclearplants)
zz<-matchit(pr ~ t1 + t2, data=nuclearplants, method = "nearest", 
distance = "mahalanobis",replace=TRUE)
zz.out<-zz$match.matrix
head(zz.out)

  1
A "I"
B "N"
C "M"
D "V"
E "X"
F "


zz$distance


  [1] NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA NA


I was wondering why I am having NA values for the output distance.

Best regards,
Nayan

messages.body_plain:
Hi Nayan,
I believe that that is because there isn't a single "distance" measure that makes sense.

With Mahalanobis matching the Mahalanobis distance is calculated between each treated subject and each control (so if there are 100 treated and 200 control there are 100*200 Mahalanobis distances potentially calculated).  So there isn't just a single number that could be put in a vector, one number for each person.

Liz

messages.subject: Memory problem in Full matching
messages.body_plain:
Hi there,
I'm running full matching on a large data set (sample size is about 40,000).  There appeared an error "

In data.frame(control = factor(controls[idx]), treated =
factor(treatments[idx]),  :

Reached total
allocation of 3965Mb: see help(memory.size)

" This is because the datasets are too big and taking up too much memory. Do you know how to deal with this problem? Or do you know what packages in R can be used to deal with large dataset in MatchIt?
Thank you in advance.

Best,
Xin

usual application of full matching, but they are related.
